messages:
nora: Quick sync — Acme asked for a concise performance playbook: batching, KV/prefix caching guidance, and quantization recommendations. They want launch gates tied to p95 latency and quality regressions. Can we scope a PRD and clear acceptance criteria?
maya: High level proposal: split into 3 deliverables. M1: 'Rules of Thumb' + validated runbook. M2: Console suggester (automated config hints). M3: API/infra for canary rollouts + eval hooks. Acceptance criteria idea below. :thinking_face:
sam: Technical constraints to call out: quantization profiles differ by model & workload. Need a fidelity check step in the pipeline (e.g., LM evals on prompt set) before enabling q8/q4 on production. Also prefix/KV cache warmup impacts p95 numbers.
liam: Platform asks: we need telemetry contract (per-route token breakdown, quant flag, batch size). Also rollout primitives: canary percent, automatic rollback on eval delta > X. Without that we can't meet enterprise SLAs.
gautam: Edge cases we must list in PRD: very short prompt workloads (<=32 tokens) where batching harms latency; heterogeneous request lengths causing head-of-line latency; models with non-deterministic cacheable prefixes. Also network noise on Private deployments — include fallback to hosted variant.
nora: Draft acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Perf: validated p95 <= 120ms on dataset A (3 representative customer workloads) with batch/quant configs applied.
- Cost: >=20% token-cost reduction vs baseline for those workloads.
- Quality: no regression > 2% on evaluation metric (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM eval) across prompt set.
- Observability: per-route telemetry + alerting for quantized model QPS spike or cache miss rate > 30%.
- Rollout: ability to canary to 1% then auto-rollback on quality regressions.
maya: Love that. For PRD sections: Goals, Non-goals, Acceptance Criteria (above), Stakeholders, Customer asks (Acme + 2 others), Implementation plan, Launch checklist. Can we add a short 'Decision log' for model-specific quantization choices?
sam: Implementation notes: we should include a small matrix example in PRD showing model X, profile Y, expected p95/cost delta. Example:```
model: redwood-7B
profile: q4_0
expected_p95: 140ms
cost_delta: -28%
quality_delta: -0.6%
```
This helps sales/SE set expectations.
liam: Also add operational gates: when cache hit rate < 50% we disable batching auto-burst; when quant quality delta > threshold, revert to FP. These are simple rules we can implement in runtime.
gautam: Customer-driven asks to record: Acme wants a config export that SEs can check into their IaC; Beta customers want CLI tools to run local sims. Add those to M2 backlog.
maya: Who owns PRD writeup? Nora + Sam take initial draft. Liam to add rollout & telemetry pieces. Gautam to write edge-case appendix. I'll schedule a 30m review with Acme SEs next Tue.
ops-bot: New doc created: https://redwood.internal/docs/optkit/2061234567-playbook-draft — editing permissions: eng-ml, eng-platform, product. :white_check_mark:
nora: Cool. Next steps: Nora/Sam to post PRD draft by EOD Thursday, tag stakeholders. If anyone has an objection to acceptance criteria numbers, call it out now. :thumbsup:
sam: Small ask: can we relax p95 target for tiny models (<1B) to 180ms? Cold starts kill us there. Otherwise :+1:
liam: Agreed — add per-class SLOs in PRD (small/medium/large model buckets).
maya: Noted. I'll add a line in PRD for per-model SLO buckets and explicit beta acceptance for Private deployments.
gautam: I'll add two tests for edge-cases: short-prompt workload and variable-length bursts. Will mock telemetry in staging.
nora: Great — thanks everyone. I'll upload the draft and ping for review.
maya: :rocket:
